styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: The Alcázar, the cathedral and the Santa Cruz lanes.

styles.label: Tapas
styles.blurb: Bar-hopping, market snacks and long tapas dinners.

styles.label: Flamenco
styles.blurb: Live flamenco shows in Triana and the old town.

stays.why: Walk to the Alcázar, the cathedral and the narrow lanes; very atmospheric, but streets are tight and quiet at night.
Across the river from the old town, with tapas bars and flamenco tablaos; a short walk to the centre.
Near the bullring and the river, a short walk to Santa Cruz and the cathedral; busy and convenient.
Local neighbourhood north of the old town, with lower prices; a longer walk or bus ride to the main sights.

food: Eat tapas in small bars: order a few plates to share, such as jamón, croquetas and pimientos de padrón.
Try the bars in Triana along Calle Betis and across the river for lively, local-style evenings.
Eat late: many locals dine after 21:00, so kitchens may be quieter before then.
Pick a sit-down café or bar for breakfast with toast and coffee, usually cheaper than a full meal (check prices on the day).
Ask for the menu del día at lunch for a set meal at a good price (check on the day).
more_time: Take a day trip to Córdoba by train to see the Mezquita and its historic old town.
Visit Itálica, the Roman ruins just outside Seville, for a quieter half-day.
Spend an afternoon at the Plaza de España and Parque de María Luisa for gardens and riverside walks.

recommend.why: Two nights give you time for the Alcázar, the cathedral, a flamenco show and a tapas evening without rushing.

month_notes: Jan: Mild and cool, 6–16°C with 5 rainy days. Good for sightseeing.
Feb: Mild, 8–18°C with 4 rainy days. Quiet and pleasant.
Mar: Warm spring, 10–21°C, with the most rain days (10). Pack a light umbrella.
Apr: Pleasant, 12–23°C with 7 rainy days. Great for walking.
May: Warm, 15–29°C and mostly dry (4 rainy days). Ideal, but busy.
Jun: Very hot, 19–33°C with almost no rain. Plan indoor visits midday.
Jul: Extremely hot, 22–37°C and dry. Go out early or after dark.
Aug: Extremely hot, 22–37°C and dry. Same as July; keep midday for shade.
Sep: Still hot, 19–32°C with 3 rainy days. Evenings start to cool.
Oct: Comfortable, 16–27°C with 7 rainy days. A strong month to visit.
Nov: Mild, 11–20°C with 7 rainy days. Good for walking and tapas.
Dec: Cool, 8–17°C with 6 rainy days. Good for culture, with some rain.

climate_guide.summary: Hot, dry summers and mild, sunny winters. Spring and autumn are the best times to walk the old city.

items.title: Best time: March to May and October to November
items.text: Mild days, roughly 16–27°C, and comfortable evenings. Best for walking and outdoor tapas.

items.title: Summer is extreme (June to August)
items.text: Highs reach about 33–37°C with almost no rain. Visit sights early, rest midday and go out again after dark.

items.title: Rain is mostly in winter and spring
items.text: Rainy days cluster from October to March, with the most in March. Showers are usually short.

items.title: Cool winter evenings
items.text: December to February can dip to about 6–8°C at night. Bring a jacket for evening walks.

items.title: Strong sun, even in spring
items.text: Sun is strong from April. Use sunscreen, a hat and water, and seek shade in the middle of the day.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes for summer, layers for winter, comfortable walking shoes for cobbled streets, and a small umbrella for spring and autumn.

transit.best: Walk the old town, since the main sights are compact. Use buses or taxis for longer trips.

modes.text: One line runs south-west to south-east and misses the old town. Tickets cost €1.30 for one zone.
City buses are frequent and cover most of the city. A single fare is €1.40, or €0.35–0.38 with a rechargeable bonobus card.
Taxis are easy to find. Cabify, Uber, Bolt and FreeNow all operate, and Cabify is the local favourite. Check the fare before you ride.
Driving in the old city is tricky. Park in a hotel garage, and never leave anything in the car because break-ins are common.
Walking is the best way to see the sights, since the main points are compact.
Trams run about 2 km from Prado de San Sebastián to Plaza Nueva, past the cathedral. Most visitors walk this stretch instead.
Sevici bikes and Lime scooters are available around the city.
